root_idea.summary: The root centers on the right hand and right-hand side, with associated extensions to strength, blessing, felicity, oath, and possession or authority.
root_idea.development: The semantic development proceeds from the right hand and right side to auspiciousness and blessing, the oath associated with clasping right hands, and possession or authority expressed through the right hand. The same orientation also underlies the geographic name Yemen and related demonyms and products.

senses.definition: Right; situated on or associated with the right-hand side.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally in the supplied Quranic occurrences for the right side or direction.

senses.definition: The right-hand side or right-associated company; in the Quran, the blessed party on the right.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for those associated with the right, where right-hand orientation carries an association with felicity and blessing.

senses.definition: The right hand; by extension, the right-hand side or direction.
senses.usage_conditions: Covers literal hand references and directional expressions such as being or acting at the right.

senses.definition: A forceful taking or seizure by the right hand, hence restraint, repulsion, or prevention.
senses.usage_conditions: Attested in the Quranic construction of taking someone by the right hand to prevent or overpower them.

senses.definition: The right-associated party: people of felicity, blessing, or good fortune.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in expressions such as أصحاب اليمين, where the right is conventionally associated with felicity and blessing.

senses.definition: An oath; a covenant or commitment confirmed by an oath.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for sworn undertakings and their confirmation, including covenants expressed or ratified by oath.

senses.definition: Right-hand possession or authority; those under such possession or authority.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic possession construction مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ, the right hand is a metonym for possession or authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be prosperous, fortunate, or lucky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I verb expressing good fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something incline or turn toward the right.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use describing the direction into which something is made to incline.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be placed on one's right side in the grave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized physical or funerary use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or derive blessing or good fortune from something; to regard it as auspicious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a source of blessing such as counsel, a word, or speech; opposed to regarding something as ominous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prosperity, good fortune, luck, or auspiciousness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for favorable fortune, contrasted with ill luck or misfortune.
A directional use distinct from the ordinary meanings of right side and oath.
A nisbah-based designation for a Yemeni garment.
A classical adjectival branch distinct from the Quran-attested directional sense of أَيْمَنُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A singular noun used in swearing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used only in oath formulas; it is not a particle or a plural of يَمِينٌ and is derived from يُمْنٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The right wing of an army.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A military formation term; this specialization is broader Classical Arabic evidence, not a claim about the Quranic contexts.
An adjectival description of a person or thing characterized by good fortune or blessing.
A verbal noun for the experience or acquisition of blessing.

cautions: أَيْمَنُ is Quran-attested here in the directional sense “right”; its separately attested Classical Arabic sense “lucky” is kept outside the Quranic sense.
For يَمِينٌ, “rightfully” in possession contexts is a constructional rendering of right-hand possession or authority, not a separate basic hand meaning.
The forceful seizure sense is tied to the Quranic construction of taking someone by the right hand and should not be generalized to every occurrence of يَمِينٌ.
